items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-16): the Plaid sync insert at apps/api/src/plaid/sync.ts:95-103 uses `ON CONFLICT(plaid_transaction_id) DO NOTHING`, but db.ts:292-294 creates that index as PARTIAL (`... WHERE plaid_transaction_id IS NOT NULL`). Verified against the project's own better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers build with the production schema: the bare conflict target fails at PREPARE time with SQLITE_ERROR 'ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint'. applyAdded therefore throws on the first page containing added rows; syncItem's catch (sync.ts:78-82) swallows it into status='error' and the cursor update at :72-74 is skipped, so the page replays and fails forever and Plaid rows never land. Fix: add the index predicate to the conflict target (`ON CONFLICT(plaid_transaction_id) WHERE plaid_transaction_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`) and add a behavioral test that prepares the real statement against a migrated in-memory DB. NOTE: fixing this alone exposes finance-product-dedupe-04 (pending-to-posted natural-key collision) - do both together. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.

items.evidence: apps/api/src/merchant.ts:14; apps/api/src/server.ts:487; apps/api/src/rules-engine.ts:74-75
items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-16, CHRONIC runsOpen 7): merchants whose descriptors carry a per-order token normalize to a unique string per transaction, so the categorization tail never shrinks for them. merchant.ts:14 strips `/\*+\d+/g`, which requires digits immediately after the asterisk. Executed against the shipped normalizer: 'AMZN Mktp US*2X4RT8901' -> 'AMZN MKTP US X4RT8901' and 'AMZN Mktp US*9K7QQ1122' -> 'AMZN MKTP US K7QQ1122' - it eats only the leading digit and leaves the order token attached. Every such transaction becomes its own Categorize row and, with the default-on save-as-rule, writes an exact-string rule (server.ts:487 stores body.merchant verbatim) that can never match another transaction, growing the rules table without shrinking the tail. Same class: 'SQ *', 'TST*', 'PAYPAL *'. Fix: strip the full alphanumeric token after an aggregator prefix (and any trailing alphanumeric order-id run) in normalizeMerchant so 'AMZN MKTP US' collapses to one merchant and one rule. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.
items.notes: 2026-07-17T02:36Z queue-drain-hourly: FIRST verification (never-attempted). CONFIRMED REAL - core claim and conclusion both hold, with two wording corrections worth carrying into the fix. (1) merchant.ts:14 does ship /\*+\d+/g. Executed the shipped normalizer verbatim: 'AMZN Mktp US*2X4RT8901' -> 'AMZN MKTP US X4RT8901' and 'AMZN Mktp US*9K7QQ1122' -> 'AMZN MKTP US K7QQ1122'. Both match the finding exactly - the pattern eats only the leading digit and leaves the order token attached, so every such transaction is its own merchant. (2) server.ts:483-487 does store body.merchant verbatim as the rule pattern (is_regex=0, match_field='normalizedMerchant'), and save-as-rule IS default-on (Categorize.tsx:27 useState(true)). So the unbounded rules-table growth is real. CORRECTION A: the finding calls the result an 'exact-string rule'; rules-engine.ts:73-76 actually matches by SUBSTRING (haystack.toUpperCase().includes(rule.upperPattern)), not exact equality. The conclusion is unchanged - a pattern carrying a per-order token can never be a substring of a different order's descriptor - but a fix that assumes exact-match semantics would be wrong. CORRECTION B: the 'same class: SQ *, TST*, PAYPAL *' claim does NOT reproduce as stated. Executed: 'SQ *COFFEE BAR SEATTLE WA' -> 'SQ COFFEE BAR', 'PAYPAL *STEAM GAMES' -> 'PAYPAL STEAM GAMES' - both collapse cleanly and are NOT affected. 'TST* PIZZA PLACE 4471' -> 'TST PIZZA PLACE 4471' retains a store number (the /\s+#\d+/ pattern only strips it when written '#4471'), which is stable per store and so does not grow the tail per-transaction. The bug is specific to descriptors carrying a PER-ORDER token, not to aggregator prefixes generally - scoping the fix to 'any aggregator prefix' would over-collapse distinct merchants (every SQ * merchant would fold into one). Repo state: HEAD a962350 (moved since the 2026-07-16 note's ba2ae66), working tree CLEAN. NOT APPLIED: auto_safe:false and the prompt says ship via scripts/release.ps1 = publishing, which is out of this task's no-publish scope. Kept PENDING for an attended YaB session. Fix is now de-risked: strip a trailing per-order alphanumeric run (require it to look like an order id - mixed letters+digits, length >= 6) rather than blanket-stripping the token after any '*', keep substring semantics in mind, and add a normalizer unit test covering both the AMZN collapse and the SQ */PAYPAL * non-regression before shipping.

items.evidence: apps/api/src/backup.ts:100-116 (pruneOldBackups), :126-141 + server.ts:1227-1235 (pruneIfDue on every boot)
items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-16, CHRONIC runsOpen 7): backup creation is purely event-driven (import/rollback/manual/plaid-takeover only) while deletion is unconditional and time-driven - pruneIfDue(30) fires on every api boot and pruneOldBackups (backup.ts:100-116) is mtime-only with no keep-newest-N floor. Any user who does not import for 30 days converges to zero backups. That is the steady state RIGHT NOW: X:\YesAndBudget\data\backups\ and X:\.budget\backups\ both contain 0 .db files, while data/yesandbudget.db is 548864 bytes with a current mtime. backup.test.ts:78-92 pins the prune behavior but never asserts a survivor floor. Fix: add a keep-at-least-3-newest floor to pruneOldBackups so it can never empty the directory, and add a periodic snapshot (boot-time createBackup('daily') gated by a meta day-key, mirroring pruneIfDue) so cadence does not depend on import frequency. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.
items.notes: 2026-07-17T04:40Z queue-drain-hourly: FIRST verification (never-attempted). CONFIRMED REAL on all four claims, read-only, no fix applied (auto_safe:false + this task is no-publish). items.title: Drive the Plaid takeover archive boundary from Plaid's real earliest_available_date so post-takeover history cannot double-count
items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-10): PlaidConnectFlow.tsx:92-94 hard-codes the takeover window to exactly 90 days back, with an in-code comment conceding "Phase 2 should ask Plaid for the real earliest_available_date". commitTakeover (plaid/takeover.ts:65-78) therefore archives CSV rows only WHERE posted_date >= that date, one-shot and never re-run, while Plaid backfills up to 24 months of the same history as source='plaid' (plaid/sync.ts:85-121 re-archives nothing). Neither unique index catches the overlap: CSV raw_description differs from the Plaid name, and CSV rows carry a NULL plaid_transaction_id. Every real transaction older than 90 days therefore appears twice in transactions_live and double-counts in all analytics. Fix: drive the archive boundary from Plaid's real earliest_available_date per item, or re-archive overlapping live CSV rows on each sync as older Plaid history backfills. Add a regression test covering a takeover with CSV rows predating the window. Live exposure is limited today because Plaid is Sandbox-only (D-012), but this bites the moment Production is approved. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.

items.title: The five-webhook block in every handler is boilerplate; only 1-4 of 5 URL files exist per project
items.detail: Every handler ships a near-identical Discord block promising five '<identifier> <Role> Bot' webhooks with five URL files under X:\.secrets\<Project>\scripts\. Actual files on disk: Hordes 1/5 (.discord_webhook.txt only), Chains 1/5, Scheduler 3/5, Apothecary 3/5, Budget 4/5, Rising 4/5 (missing resources). Ring has resources plus a .revoked-2026-06-30 sibling. Gnosis uses a different content-webhook set entirely (characters/items/maps/monsters/one-shot-ideas). items.title: photos storage bucket is enumerable by any client; exposes pending (unscreened) catteries' photos
items.detail: X:\YesAndCattery\supabase\migrations\0006_photos_storage_bucket.sql declares `create policy "photos public read" on storage.objects for select using (bucket_id = 'photos')`. A select policy on storage.objects governs LISTING, not just object fetches. The bucket is already public, so objects serve by URL without any policy - this policy buys nothing for display but lets any client call the storage list API and enumerate every object. Supabase security advisor flags it as public_bucket_allows_listing (WARN). Impact is project-specific: a cattery is deliberately not public until screened, yet photos are uploaded during the pending application, so enumeration exposes unscreened catteries' photos that RLS otherwise hides. Fix: drop or scope the broad select policy (e.g. restrict to owner + screened-cattery paths), confirm app.js display paths use direct public object URLs and never the list API, then re-run get_advisors(security) to confirm the lint clears. Note this policy also lives only in a repo file that was never applied through prod migration history (see canonical-audit-2026-07-02-cattery-missing-migrations) - the live bucket policy must be changed in prod too, not just in the file.

items.title: .project-context.json changelog_path points at a CHANGELOG.md that does not exist
items.detail: X:\YesAndSkylight\.project-context.json sets "changelog_path": "CHANGELOG.md", but no CHANGELOG.md exists at the repo root and never has. Skylight tracks releases by version-lockstep (DESIGN.md header + package.json + src/version.ts, all 0.2.0) rather than a changelog file, so the pointer is a phantom. Low impact -- nothing reads it today -- but any tooling that trusts .project-context.json (YaE status/usage-attribution, bar-raise) would resolve a missing path. Fix is a judgment call between two options: (a) drop the changelog_path key entirely, matching the actual version-lockstep convention documented in DESIGN.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md "Parity rules"; or (b) create a real CHANGELOG.md and start maintaining it. Recommend (a) -- the lockstep convention is deliberate and documented, and a changelog nobody writes is worse than none. NOT auto-applied: .project-context.json is co-owned (YaE usage-attribution + bar-raise routines also write it) and this is a convention decision, not a text-alignment fix. BOOKKEEPING NOTE: this item is the long-carried audit finding S4. The CANONICAL_AUDIT reports of 2026-07-02 onward (through 07-15) each listed it as pending under exactly this queue id, but it was never actually written to the queue -- the id was cited without the enqueue landing. Verified absent from the queue on 2026-07-16 and enqueued then under the previously-cited id so the existing report references resolve.

items.title: Character gate's soft/hard viewing model lives only in a code comment: hidden_from is not a gate and the spec never says so
items.detail: The site-wide character gate shipped in v0.3.19x (commit 66d2aec) and introduces a SECOND, weaker tier of hiding alongside secret:. PROJECT_SPEC.md and CLAUDE.md both contain zero mentions of: character gate, identity gate, hidden_from, /api/whoami, /dm-logout, gnosis-char, or /map-aestaria. The distinction between the two tiers is recorded only in a build.mjs code comment (line 1688): hidden_from is a client-side courtesy filter whose hidden text SHIPS IN THE HTML, while secret: is a hard worker-side gate. The implementation is correct and the comment is honest; the gap is that neither fact reaches the canonical doc every session is told to read first. Not a live exposure: zero vault files currently use hidden_from and the secret: gate is intact and verified (126 entities gated, search index redacted, questions board clean). The risk is the armed trap: the first time someone puts spoiler-bearing content behind hidden_from believing it is a gate, it ships to every player. Suggested: document the two-tier model in section 3 (frontmatter contract, next to the secret: rules) and section 6 (as the locked decision it plainly is). Needs Kane's wording; the substance is already settled by the code.
items.notes: Doc gap, not a live leak. Cheap to close now, expensive after the first hidden_from use.

items.title: Section 5 milestone stamp drifted twice in two days and went factually inverted; stop hand-maintaining the counts
items.detail: The v0.3 milestone stamp in section 5 carries hand-maintained entity/pin/location counts. It was refreshed on 2026-07-16 and was stale again within 24 hours (485 -> 574 entities). Worse, yesterday's refresh introduced a factual inversion: it read '81 pins rendered from the 86 of 108 locations that carry PUBLIC map: coordinates', but 86 is the SECRET Aestaria pin count, not the public one (actual: 167 of 181 locations carry coordinates, 81 public / 86 secret, 15 opt out with map: none). A doc describing the redaction contract asserted the opposite of the redaction reality. The 2026-07-17 pass corrected the digits and added a line pointing at build.mjs output as authoritative, but the underlying problem stands: a hand-maintained count cannot survive a project ingesting ~90 entities a day, and each refresh is a fresh chance to invert a fact. Suggested: recast the stamp as build-derived language and drop the digits entirely (e.g. 'build.mjs prints current entity, pin, and broken-link counts on every run'). Not auto-applied because dropping information from a canonical milestone is a scope call. Needs Kane.

items.evidence: worker/src/handlers/billing.js:656-690 (checkout.session.completed branch; no payment_status gate, no event.id dedupe, no stripe_subscription_id persisted, 200-ACKs a missing profile)
items.prompt: Yes& Chains [HIGH, bar-raise finding webhook-01]: the Stripe webhook handler is under-hardened on a live money path. At worker/src/handlers/billing.js:656-690 the checkout.session.completed branch does not gate on payment_status == "paid" (so an unpaid or async-pending session can grant Pro), does not dedupe on event.id (Stripe retries at-least-once, so replays re-apply), does not persist stripe_subscription_id (which dataint-01 reconciliation and finance-02 dunning both need), and 200-ACKs when the profile lookup misses, silently discarding the grant with no retry. Fix all four: gate on payment_status, add an idempotency table or KV key on event.id, store stripe_subscription_id, and return a non-2xx on a missing profile so Stripe retries. Pairs with dataint-01. items.evidence: server.mjs:549, inside POST /script, builds the command "Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue '.git\index.lock'; & '<scriptPath>'" and runs it with cwd set to the TARGET repo. CLAUDE.md:30 forbids exactly this ("never blind-Remove-Item it") and mandates git-guard.ps1 Assert-GitSafe before any git write. Worse than a skipped guard: the delete runs immediately before invoking release.ps1 / push-to-github.ps1, which DO call Assert-GitSafe (push-to-github.ps1:7,40,45,70 + Confirm-GitIntact:74; write-dashboard-status.ps1:20,135,139,144,146). Their guard then finds no lock, concludes there is no race, and proceeds - so the preamble launders a live race into a clean-looking one and disables the abort path at git-guard.ps1:29-38. git-guard.ps1's own header records the damage this race has already caused: NUL-truncated .git\config and refs/heads/main knocked out of loose refs. Blast radius is cross-project: /script runs against any allowlisted repo (HBH, YaC, Gnosis, ...), and the portfolio runs concurrent unattended routines by design.
items.title: Agents /script blind-deletes .git\index.lock in the target repo, defeating the git-guard the handler mandates
items.prompt: Canonical audit 2026-07-24 (HIGH). X:\YesAndAgents server.mjs:549: the POST /script handler prefixes every run with "Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue '.git\index.lock'" in the target repo's cwd, then invokes that repo's release.ps1 or push-to-github.ps1. This violates CLAUDE.md:30 (never blind-Remove-Item the lock; use Assert-GitSafe from scripts/git-guard.ps1) and neutralises the guard inside the scripts it calls - they see a clean tree and skip the wait-then-abort logic that exists for exactly this race. DO: delete the Remove-Item preamble so the command is just "& '<scriptPath>'". The invoked scripts already clear genuinely-stale locks correctly via Assert-GitSafe, so the preamble is redundant with a safer implementation that already runs; removing it restores the abort. VERIFY: read scripts/git-guard.ps1 (Assert-GitSafe waits up to 20s for a live git process, then throws rather than writing into the race) and confirm push-to-github.ps1 still calls it on entry. DECISION for the implementer: whether /script should catch a guard abort and stream it to the phone as a distinct, readable error, or just let the script's throw stream through as ordinary stderr. auto_safe=false: it is a behaviour change on the remote-ship path plus a small UX call, so it wants an eyeball and a real /script run against a clean repo before shipping.

Every check is a human re-grep performed by the nightly canonical audit, which is why the audit report spends its first screen re-proving the same four facts. node:test is a Node builtin, so a test file breaches nothing in D-004. Fix: add a single test file (run with 'node --test') asserting that server.mjs deletes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at all three spawn sites, that BIND_HOST defaults to 127.0.0.1 and the non-local-without-password path exits, that MODELS excludes fable and every spawn passes an explicit --model (D-008), that no package.json exists, and that no prompt string reaches argv. Then the nightly audit can cite a green run instead of re-deriving it, and a regression becomes impossible to ship silently.

items.evidence: server.mjs:296 - ip = String(req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] || req.socket.remoteAddress).split(',')[0].trim(), with no trusted-proxy check; loginFails is keyed on that value (server.mjs:220-228)
items.prompt: Agents MEDIUM (bar-raise 2026-07-24): the login rate-limit and five-failure lockout key on the first entry of a caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For header with no trusted-proxy check, so a caller who can reach the port can defeat the lockout entirely by rotating the header between attempts. Impact is bounded today because the server binds 127.0.0.1, the only ingress is the Cloudflare tunnel, and Cloudflare Access default-deny on a single email sits in front - an attacker has to get through Access before the password page exists at all. That is defense in depth working as designed, which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH, but the innermost layer currently contributes less than it appears to. Fix: trust the forwarded header only when the request carries a cf-ray (i.e. genuinely arrived through the tunnel) and prefer cf-connecting-ip when it does; otherwise key the limiter on req.socket.remoteAddress. Same pattern the /healthz caller check at server.mjs:282-290 already uses, so it is consistent with code that is already there.
